statement: For subgroups G_1..G_k of finite index in any group G, letting N be the intersection of the cores of the G_i, G/N is finite and a family of cosets x_1G_1,...,x_kG_k is pairwise disjoint in G iff the corresponding cosets are pairwise disjoint in G/N, with the same indices n_i; hence WLOG G is finite.
If [G:G_i] and [G:G_j] are coprime finite indices then xG_i and yG_j intersect for every x,y in G; hence in a pairwise disjoint family gcd(n_i,n_j) >= 2 for every i<j.
For a pairwise disjoint family of finite-index cosets x_1G_1,...,x_kG_k, sum_i 1/n_i <= 1.

If gcd(n_i,n_j) in {2,3,4,5} for all pairs among n_1..n_6 (necessary for a k=6 counterexample by Lemma 2 plus the counterexample condition gcd<=5), then writing D_i = {p in {2,3,5}: p|n_i}, every D_i is nonempty and |D_i cap D_j| = 1 for all i != j.

Exhaustive search over all 7^6=117649 assignments D:{1..6}->{nonempty subsets of {2,3,5}} finds exactly 147 valid tuples (|D_i cap D_j|=1 for all pairs), collapsing to exactly 4 patterns up to the S_6 x S_3 symmetry (relabel indices, relabel primes).

statement: Each of the 4 shared-prime patterns for a k=6 candidate can be realized by explicit integers n_1..n_6 with every pairwise gcd in {2,3,4,5} and sum 1/n_i <= 1 (using distinct large prime cofactors coprime to 2,3,5), so the density bound (iii) never by itself excludes any of the 4 patterns.

Lemmas 1-3 and the 4-pattern classification give only necessary numeric conditions on the indices n_1..n_6 of a hypothetical k=6 group-form counterexample; they do not construct or rule out an actual group G with subgroups of these indices and pairwise disjoint cosets, so k=6 for the group form remains open after this task.

For each of the 4 numeric patterns (I-IV in result.md), attempt to construct an actual finite group G with subgroups G_1..G_6 of matching indices and pairwise disjoint cosets x_1G_1,...,x_6G_6, or prove no such construction exists for that pattern.

Refine the 4-pattern classification by also tracking the exponent of the shared prime 2 (v_2=1 giving gcd 2, vs v_2>=2 giving gcd 4) to get a finer necessary condition for realizability, and check whether any refinement is incompatible with known small-group coset structures.
